html:
Sticky (glutinous) rice is the staple food of Laos, eaten by hand from small woven baskets at almost every meal. Lao people eat more of it per person than anyone else on Earth.

It is steamed, not boiled, and rolled into balls to scoop up dishes such as laap, a minced meat salad, and jaew, a chilli dip. It is also the staple of Isan in northeast Thailand, settled by Lao people after the revolt of Anouvong.

Lao people sometimes call themselves children of sticky rice. Rice growing in the region goes back thousands of years; see rice at Khok Phanom Di. See also Mekong.
